svg.title: a freshly generated project passes its own quality gate: Trivy skips the folders its settings list and still reports the project's own dependencies
svg.text: a freshly generated project passes its own quality gate
Scenario: Trivy skips the folders its settings list and still reports the project's own dependencies

g.text: Given a generated project holds the same vulnerable lockfile at its root and in a library
A project generated from the toolbox holds the same lockfile twice. package-lock.json, at the root, lists the project's
own dependencies. vendor/acme/widget/package-lock.json stands for a library a package manager installed under vendor/.
Both pin lodash 4.17.20, a version with a known vulnerability.
When the developer scans the project with Trivy's settings, it reports the root lockfile and
Trivy scans the project with its settings file and saves what it finds as JSON. jq, a JSON reader, then lists the files
in which Trivy found a vulnerability.
There is one: package-lock.json, the project's own lockfile. vendor/acme/widget/package-lock.json pins the same lodash
4.17.20 and is not listed: Trivy skipped the vendor folder.
Then Trivy's settings file lists the folders to skip and still points to
The settings file MegaLinter hands Trivy. Its scan.skip-dirs list names vendor next to the
other folders that hold no code of the project's own, such as .cache, .git and venv. Trivy
reads the list from this file.
Its ignorefile line still points Trivy to trivyignore.yml, the file of findings the project
